newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Two die, 20 injured in Mideast quake.
newsitem.headline: Two die, 20 injured in Mideast quake.

text.p: Two people died, 20 were injured and hundreds of tourists fled swaying hotels on Wednesday when a powerful tremor hit the east Mediterranean region.
Egyptian security sources said Adeela Rabea al-Gaafari died in Faheem village, in the Delta province of Gharbiya, when the earthquake destroyed her one-storey home.
Cyprus police said a 73-year-old man died of a heart attack as he and other patients were escorted downstairs at Limassol General Hospital during the tremor.
The earthquake hit Egypt at about 3.15 pm (1315 GMT) and measured about six on the Richter scale, state-run television said. It was also felt in Israel, Lebanon, Syria and Turkey.

In Cyprus, police said some 20 people were slightly injured in the coastal resort of Paphos as they rushed to leave buildings during the one minute tremor. Hundreds of tourists evacuated their hotels.
Cyprus Radio's Paphos correspondent reported:"People in the commercial district ran into the streets. Drivers left the motors in their cars running and abandoned them."
In Cyprus the earthquake measured between 6.2 and 6.5 on the Richter scale, Cypriot seismologist Kyriakos Solomis told Reuters.
"Its epicentre was 40 km (25 miles) south-west of Cyprus in the Paphos area," Solomis said.
There was minor damage to buildings in Paphos and the nearby port city of Limassol. Landslides were also reported in south-west Cyprus.
A Limassol police spokesman said:"We are going crazy, there is plenty of damage."
The Cyprus Geological Survey said there were more than 100 after shocks measuring between 3.5 and 5.5 on the Richter scale.
The region is no stranger to earthquakes.
Six people died, including two who jumped out of buildings in panic, and 10 others were hurt after an earthquake hit Egypt last year.
More than 500 people died and hundreds were hurt and left homeless when a strong earthquake hit Egypt on October 12, 1992. Most injuries occurred when badly constructed buildings collapsed.
The Paphos area was hit by an earthquake meauring 5.2 on the Richter scale in February 1995. Two elderly people were killed when their house collapsed.
In 1953, 64 people were killed when an earthquake hit Paphos.
